modules.desc: Docker is a baseline skill for DevOps, backend, cloud and SRE roles. It appears in the vast majority of modern job descriptions.

modules.title: Ends "works on my machine"
modules.desc: Containers bundle your app and its dependencies, so it runs identically on every machine, every time.

modules.title: The gateway to Kubernetes
modules.desc: Containers are the foundation of Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines and cloud-native architecture. Docker is step one.

modules.title: Fast to get productive
modules.desc: You can learn the core workflow in an afternoon and start containerizing real apps the same day.

faqs.question: Is this Docker course really free?+
faqs.answer: Yes. Every lesson and the interactive playground are 100% free, with no sign-up, no paywall and no downloads required.

faqs.question: Do I need programming experience to learn Docker?+
faqs.answer: No. Basic comfort with a command line helps, but the fundamentals lessons start from zero and explain every concept along the way.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn Docker?+
faqs.answer: You can grasp the core workflow, images, containers, and the essential commands, in a few hours. Working through this full path with the playground takes roughly a weekend.

faqs.question: What is the best way to learn Docker?+
faqs.answer: By doing. Read a concept, then immediately practice the command. This path pairs short lessons with a hands-on browser playground so knowledge sticks.

faqs.question: Do I need to install Docker to practice?+
faqs.answer: Not to start. The interactive playground simulates Docker in your browser, so you can practice real commands before installing anything locally.

modules.desc: Kubernetes is the de-facto way to run containers in production, powering everything from startups to the largest tech companies.

modules.title: One of the highest-paid skills
modules.desc: Kubernetes consistently ranks among the most in-demand and best-paid skills for DevOps, platform and SRE engineers.

modules.title: Self-healing & scalable by design
modules.desc: Declare the desired state once and Kubernetes keeps it true. Restarting failed pods and scaling to meet demand automatically.

modules.title: Cloud-portable
modules.desc: The same manifests run on any cluster, local, AWS, GCP or Azure, so your skills and workloads travel with you.

faqs.question: Is this Kubernetes course really free?+
faqs.answer: Yes. Every lesson and the interactive kubectl playground are 100% free, with no sign-up, no paywall and no downloads required.

faqs.question: Should I learn Docker before Kubernetes?+
faqs.answer: A little Docker helps because Kubernetes runs containers, but you can start here. Understanding images and containers first makes pods and deployments click faster.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn Kubernetes?+
faqs.answer: You can grasp the core objects, pods, deployments and services, in a few hours. Working through this full path with the playground takes roughly a weekend.

faqs.question: What is the best way to learn Kubernetes?+
faqs.answer: By doing. Read a concept, then immediately run the kubectl command. This path pairs short lessons with a hands-on browser playground so the knowledge sticks.

faqs.question: Do I need to install Kubernetes to practice?+
faqs.answer: Not to start. The interactive playground simulates a Kubernetes cluster in your browser, so you can practice real kubectl commands before installing minikube or kind locally.

modules.title: Learn once, use everywhere
modules.desc: The same commands work on your laptop, on a Raspberry Pi, inside a container and on a fleet of cloud servers. Linux skills transfer to every environment you will ever touch.

modules.title: Automate the boring parts
modules.desc: Bash scripting turns repetitive tasks into a single command. Once you can pipe, filter and script, you stop clicking and start automating.

modules.title: Fast to get productive
modules.desc: You can learn to navigate, manage files and search text in an afternoon, and start feeling at home in any terminal the same day.

faqs.answer: No. The fundamentals lessons start from zero, no prior command-line experience is assumed. You build up gradually from your first command to scripting and system administration.
